slides.title: My own timeline
slides.notes: Put three events from your own life in order. Notes: ask learners to draw a baby picture, a first day at school and today, then order them on a string line and use the words before, after and now in a spoken sentence.

slides.title: Then and now
slides.notes: Tell how a long-ago object differs from a modern one and use a simple timeline. Notes: compare an oil lamp with an electric bulb; place both on a line marked in 100-year steps and ask learners to say one way daily life changed and one way it stayed the same.

slides.title: Early civilisations and evidence
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Early civilisations and evidence
slides.notes: Describe an early river-valley civilisation and say how we know about it. Notes: sort sources into written and object, primary and secondary. Practice: a clay tablet about 4,500 years old, counted back from 2026, dates to roughly 2500 BCE; learners say what it can and cannot tell us.

slides.title: Cause, effect and change
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Cause, effect and change
slides.notes: Explain the causes and effects of one major change, such as the spread of printing. Notes: sort causes into short term and long term. Movable-type printing reached Europe around 1450, which is 576 years before 2026; learners list two effects on reading and learning.

slides.title: Sources and balanced argument
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Sources and balanced argument
slides.notes: Evaluate two sources on one event for reliability and write a balanced paragraph. Notes: take the Second World War, 1939 to 1945, and compare a diary with an official report; check who wrote it, when and why, then give one point each way before judging.

slides.title: Historiography and archives
slides.notes: Analyse competing interpretations and build an argument from primary evidence. Notes: compare two accounts of the causes of one reform or war and note what each leaves out. Practice: in a ledger of 1,200 entries, 15 per cent are damaged, so 180 are unusable; learners state what that does to the claim.

slides.title: Original research design
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Original research design
slides.notes: Design an original research question, justify method and place the findings in the wider debate. Notes: write a 300-word proposal naming sources, gaps and bias; if a sample is 80 letters from a collection of 640, that is 12.5 per cent, and learners argue whether it is representative.
